question: Who among the following sportspersons won two consecutive Olympic medals for India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**PV Sindhu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• PV Sindhu is an Indian badminton player who has won two consecutive Olympic medals.
 
• She won her **first Olympic medal, a silver, at the Rio 2016 Olympics** in the women's singles event.
 
• Sindhu secured her **second Olympic medal, a bronze, at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, held in 2021.**
 
• PV Sindhu is the first Indian woman to win two consecutive Olympic medals in badminton.
 
• Her achievements have made her one of India's most celebrated athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Badminton in India**

 
 
• Badminton is a popular sport in India, governed by the Badminton Association of India (BAI).
 
• India has produced several world-class badminton players, including Saina Nehwal, Kidambi Srikanth, and Lakshya Sen.
 
• The sport has gained prominence and support due to the success of Indian players in international competitions.
 
• Various national and international tournaments are organized in India to promote and develop badminton.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Games**
 
 
• The Olympic Games are a leading international sporting event featuring summer and winter sports competitions.
 
• The Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating every two years within the four-year period.
 
• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) oversees the organization and promotion of the Games.
 
• The Olympics aim to promote peace and unity through sportsmanship and global participation.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of Indian Athletes in the Olympics**
 
 
• India has a growing presence in the Olympic Games, with athletes winning medals in various sports.
 
• Notable Indian Olympic medalists include Abhinav Bindra (shooting), Mary Kom (boxing), and Neeraj Chopra (javelin throw).
 
• India's performance in the Olympics has improved over the years, reflecting increased investment in sports and athlete development.
 
• The Indian government and sports bodies are actively working to support and nurture talented athletes for future Olympic success.
